subject: Private deployment: runtime segmentation & ops-network alignment
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@aperturesys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy: control/data boundaries and egress constraints

Marcus / Kimberly —

Thanks for taking this on. Aperture is finalizing requirements for a private on-prem deployment of our inference workload and we want to align on the control-plane / data-plane split, egress constraints, and operational handoffs before we lock networking changes with our colo provider. High level asks: 

- We must ensure control-plane (control APIs, model management, rollouts) is reachable only from a small set of management subnets (no public endpoints).
- Data-plane (inference nodes) will run in customer racks and can initiate outbound to our telemetry/metrics endpoints over a fixed egress IP range; customer firewall rules will only allow those egress IPs.
- PCI and data residency constraints: logs must be retained in-customer for 90 days; audit logs go to an S3-compatible bucket managed by the customer and must be encrypted with their KMS.
- We need a minimal diagram showing NAT/proxying, mTLS trust anchors, and a fallback variant that uses a relay in our VPC (for customers that can't allow direct egress).

I attached Aperture's requirements doc and a quick list of blocked ports. Would appreciate a short readout and a proposed diagram or two we can present to the colo team.

Can we get a 30–45 min alignment meeting next week? Our infra lead (CC'd) is available on Nov 17–19 PST.

Thanks,
Sandeep Rao
Sr. Infra Eng — Aperture Systems

Attachments: aperture-infra-requirements.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@aperturesys.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: control/data boundaries and egress constraints

Sandeep —

Appreciate the clear list. We're available to align. Quick clarifying Qs before the call so we come prepared: 

- For the control-plane, do you require mutual TLS for controller API calls from our control plane to your management subnets, or will IP allowlisting + client certs suffice?
- For telemetry: is the requirement that metrics + traces be pushed via TLS to the customer's collector only, or is a relay option acceptable if the customer cannot expose collectors externally?
- Do you have preferred static egress IPs on your side we can document for the colo firewall? If not, we'll propose a hardened NAT pool and a fallback relay (see below).

Proposed next steps for the meeting: 1) walk the reference diagram options (direct egress vs. relay), 2) confirm cert/KMS responsibilities, 3) agree on ops runbook handoff and alert routing.

We can do Nov 17 at 10:00 PT — does that work for your infra lead? We'll bring a draft diagram and an ops-runbook template.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@aperturesys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: control/data boundaries and egress constraints

Sandeep / team —

Thanks — attaching an annotated diagram (redwood-control-data-split-v2.drawio.png) and a short note on options. High-level notes in the diagram: 

- Option A (Direct egress): inference nodes NAT through a customer-managed edge NAT box. We only require outbound 443 to the customer's collector and to the control-plane management subnets. mTLS for control-plane calls recommended; client certs can be pinned to the management subnet.

- Option B (Relay): if the customer cannot expose collectors or prefers not to maintain NAT ranges, we can run a relay in our VPC. Relay accepts TLS from nodes and forwards to Redwood-controlled telemetry ingestion. Relay is single-tenant per customer and sits behind a private peering link / VPN.

- BGP vs static routes: we prefer static routes + HA NAT for predictability unless the colo team asks for dynamic routing.

- Failure modes called out on the bottom of diagram: control-plane outage fallback (local cached model serving + degraded metrics), NAT exhaustion paths, and cert rotation windows (30-day overlap).

Attachments included: redwood-control-data-split-v2.drawio.png, ops-runbook-template.md

I'll add a one-pager on the runbook items (incident runbooks, certificate rotation steps, escalation contacts) before the meeting.

On the meeting: Nov 17 at 10:00 PT is good for us. I'll share a Drive link with the diagram in the morning.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Cloud Network, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: runtime segmentation & ops-network alignment — meeting and next steps

Sandeep / Aperture infra team —

Good meeting today, thanks for the time. Recap + action items below (short):

1) Diagrams accepted: Aperture chose Option A (direct egress via customer NAT) with an emergency Relay fallback. We'll produce a final diagram with NAT sizing notes.
2) Certs/KMS: Customer will provide a KMS ARN for log encryption and an intermediate CA for node certs. Redwood to document cert rotation steps and a 30-day overlap window.
3) Ops runbook: Redwood to draft the runbook sections on onboarding, monitoring thresholds, playbooks for NAT exhaustion, and control-plane degraded mode. Deliverable: runbook draft by Nov 24. (JIRA: INFRA-4782)
4) Network handoff: Aperture to confirm firewall rules (allowed egress IPs) by Nov 20; Redwood to provide hardened NAT pool suggestion if Aperture prefers.

Attachments we agreed to share: final diagram (after we incorporate NAT sizing), ops-runbook-template.md (we attached a starting draft), and a Drive link with the readout.

Next meeting: quick cutover dry run on Dec 2 (30 min).

If that all looks right, I'll put the runbook draft in the Drive folder and create the Jira ticket with checklist.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aperture-PrivateDeploy
